evidence_basis: project CSVs (data/processed/) + disease-model.md + Round 1 agent outputs + domain knowledge; no live literature retrieval

rubric.note: Skill-file rubric re-weighted for CDI. Measures DEVELOPMENT-PATH FEASIBILITY, not disease biology. Do not sum with the Clinical Landscape agent's score - overlapping construct.

dimensions.name: compartment_access
dimensions.definition: Does the drug reach its actual target compartment intact and free? Uses ADMET agent's C1 luminal / C2 mucosal-intracellular / C3 systemic model

dimensions.name: mechanism_validation_cdi
dimensions.definition: CDI-specific evidence strength, discounted per disease model A.3

dimensions.name: safety_package_transferability
dimensions.definition: Does existing human safety data cover the CDI dose, duration AND population

dimensions.name: formulation_cmc_gap
dimensions.definition: Marketed formulation usable as-is, or new dosage form required

dimensions.name: regulatory_path_clarity
dimensions.definition: RLD availability; 505(b)(2) vs 505(b)(1) vs BLA; exclusivity earned

dimensions.name: trial_design_precedent
dimensions.definition: Inherits add-on 3-for-3 precedent or replacement 0-for-3 precedent

dimensions.name: commercial_funding_viability
dimensions.definition: COGS, sponsor economics, generic erosion. Raised from 10% on CDI's 6-of-12 financial failure rate

rubric.veto_flag: Binary, reported separately from the weighted score. Denotes a mechanistic or clinical contradiction that a weighted average structurally cannot express.

eligibility_gate.finding: Only 3 of the 6 disease-model-flagged repurposing leads have a genuine 505(b)(2) path. Prior human exposure is not equivalent to an available Reference Listed Drug.

candidates.us_rld: UNCERTAIN - US marketing discontinued; needs formal listed-drug determination

candidates.pathway: BLA supplement - 505(b)(2) does not exist for biologics

scores.transaction_type: in-licensing (NOT a repurpose - included as reference point)
scores.key_advantage: Positive human Phase 2b - strongest clinical evidence in this report; only asset addressing Tier 1 target #70; addresses unmet need #7 (primary prevention), for which no approved option exists
scores.key_risk: Not a repurpose; BLA route; payer logic for a prevention product; sponsor Theriva stalled for funding

scores.tier1_target: #11 taurocholate-competitive germination; #66 secondary bile acid supply
scores.regulatory_pathway: 505(b)(2), IR formulation at approved dose; 3-yr exclusivity, 8-yr if QIDP granted (QIDP ARGUABLE only)
scores.positioning: Add-on to fidaxomicin/vancomycin; primary endpoint CDI recurrence through week 8
scores.key_advantage: Every non-biological barrier already cleared - RLD exists, dose within approved range, no CMC work, safety package fully transferable, add-on design has 3-for-3 precedent
scores.key_risk: Colonic free concentration may be an order of magnitude below germination IC50 (ADMET verdict C); dose ceiling ~20 mg/kg/d blocks the obvious fix because high-dose UDCA (28-30 mg/kg/d) caused harm in PSC
scores.disposition: PURSUE - Stage 0 fecal PK study first

scores.regulatory_pathway: 505(b)(2), RLD Alinia. QIDP CLEARLY eligible (it is a bona fide antibacterial) - the only 505(b)(2) candidate for which the GAIN premise straightforwardly holds
scores.key_advantage: The only candidate in the entire pipeline with existing HUMAN CDI EFFICACY DATA. Appears in disease model 4.3 (alternatives), not 4.5 (failures) - it never failed, it was never funded
scores.key_risk: It is a me-too antibacterial, the single most reliably fatal profile in CDI (4.5: 0-for-3). Its existing data support the endpoint that no longer matters (initial cure) and it is unproven on the one that does (recurrence)
scores.disposition: CONDITIONAL - reposition as add-on to fidaxomicin scored on recurrence, or drop. Realistic sponsor is NIAID, not industry

scores.key_advantage: The disease model NAMES CDCA in the #11 target row with Preclinical (strong) validation, then omits it from the A.2 repurposing list. Higher potency than UDCA. Crucially, does NOT depend on the depleted bai guild - both parent (CDCA) and metabolite (LCA) are active, so the ADMET agent's UDCA-vs-LCA effector fork is not a single point of failure here
scores.key_risk: Dose-related hepatotoxicity in a population where hepatic impairment is overrepresented (3.2); diarrhoea in ~30-40% at gallstone doses, against a diarrhoea endpoint. Also a potent FXR agonist (target #61, direction UNCERTAIN) which may shrink the bile acid pool and work against #66
scores.disposition: PURSUE as a parallel arm in the Stage 0 fecal PK study

scores.other_target: #41 v-ATPase / endosomal acidification (Module A, TcdB translocation)
scores.key_advantage: Solves the C2 compartment problem that killed ebselen and niclosamide: well absorbed, reaches the colonocyte basolaterally (no mucus layer, no dissolution step, no luminal thiol sink), and as a lipophilic weak base CONCENTRATES in acidic organelles - it accumulates in the exact compartment it must act on. Named in the model's own #41 row but missed because #41 is not Tier 1
scores.key_risk: The endosomal pH shift required to block TcdB translocation may exceed clinically achievable concentrations - unproven. QT prolongation intersects with diarrhoea-driven hypokalaemia in an elderly population
scores.disposition: ONE IN VITRO EXPERIMENT - cheapest high-information test in the whole Phase 2 analysis ($30-60k, 2-3 mo)

scores.drug: UDCA + IBAT inhibitor (odevixibat CHEMBL4297588 / maralixibat CHEMBL363392)
scores.veto_reason: ASBT is not selective for UDCA. Blocking it shunts the ENTIRE bile acid pool into the colon - including TAUROCHOLATE, the primary germinant and the very ligand at target #11 that UDCA is meant to competitively displace. Net effect on germination depends on an unmeasured ratio and could be worse than baseline. Compounded by: IBAT inhibitors' dose-limiting toxicity is diarrhoea; and combining a pennies-per-dose generic with orphan-priced on-patent drugs destroys the cost advantage while doubling the 505(b)(2) burden
scores.disposition: SURFACED, EVALUATED, REJECTED as a development path. Retained as a preclinical question for the Pathway Analyst: does IBAT inhibition raise or lower the colonic UDCA:taurocholate ratio?

scores.veto_reason: CYP3A4 substrate AND moderate inhibitor. Section 3.3's DDI checklist leads with tacrolimus, cyclosporine, warfarin, digoxin, DOACs in an elderly, renally-impaired, heavily polypharmaceutical population. Discards CDI's great pharmacological advantage (6.4: luminal drugs have near-zero DDI risk) for a preclinical-only target. Compounded by no endpoint precedent (Clinical Landscape: 'unbounded') and an approved exposure of only 3 days versus CDI's 10+
scores.disposition: DO NOT PURSUE. The 5.10 score reflects an easy pathway to a destination nobody can define - do not read it as 'middling but viable'

scores.regulatory_pathway: BLA supplement or investigator-initiated trial under IND. No 505(b)(2) exists for biologics
scores.key_advantage: 4-6 hour half-life - the effect can be switched off within a day if the infection worsens. In a disease where TNF blockade is itself a CDI risk factor, reversibility is the property that makes cytokine blockade thinkable at all. Clearly the better of the two host-directed biologics on drug-property grounds
scores.key_risk: The only plausible positioning is fulminant CDI - no endpoint precedent, 8-15 yr timelines, consent-impaired slow-accruing enrolment, cost unbounded. Daily SC injection in frail elderly. Preclinical evidence only
scores.disposition: Investigator-initiated trial only, if at all. Endpoint would be colectomy-free survival

scores.veto_reason: Targets #46 (INHIBIT IL-23) and #47 (AGONIZE IL-22) are mutually incompatible - IL-23 is the principal driver of ILC3-derived IL-22, which the disease model itself calls a protective epithelial axis. Ustekinumab would suppress the protective arm. Compounded by PK mismatch: IV induction then SC q8-12wk cannot titrate within the 8-week recurrence window
scores.clinical_signal_answer: No powered analysis is known to exist. The consistent IBD-literature signal is that ustekinumab has a LOWER SERIOUS-INFECTION RATE than anti-TNF - a statement about infections generally, not evidence of anti-CDI-recurrence efficacy. Any observational signal would be dominated by confounding by indication.
scores.disposition: NOT A DEVELOPMENT CANDIDATE. Correct action is a retrospective cohort analysis in IBD biologic registries ($100-300k, 6-9 mo) - either produces a signal or closes the question permanently

scores.regulatory_pathway: 505(b)(1) FULL NDA. No RLD exists; Phase 2 safety data belongs to other sponsors and cannot be cited without right of reference. QIDP doubtful (anti-toxin, not antibacterial)
scores.colonic_concentration_answer: Delivery is NOT the limiting step - poor solubility means most of an oral dose reaches the colon. What fails is chemical survival: (1) dissolution caps free concentration; (2) the Se-S exchange mechanism is quenched by mM cysteine/glutathione and bacterial H2S at Eh -200 mV; (3) the CPD target is intracellular (C2), so the lumen is the wrong destination anyway; (4) the systemic rescue fails identically because ebselen binds albumin Cys34 >99%. No formulation fixes a molecule consumed by the medium it must cross
scores.disposition: TOOL COMPOUND, NOT CANDIDATE. The fast path in this space belongs to the TARGET (#26), not this molecule. Hand to SAR Analyst as a warhead-replacement problem

scores.existing_formulation_answer: NO. Yomesan's 2g chewable is engineered for single-dose, purely luminal contact-killing of a tapeworm scolex - poor dissolution is a FEATURE of that product. Niclosamide's intrinsic aqueous solubility is ~1.6 uM, at or below the range where TcdB entry blockade is reported. The marketed formulation delivers mass without delivering free drug
gap_to_cdi_indication: Solubility-enabling reformulation (ASD/nanocrystal/co-crystal/prodrug) = new dosage form 505(b)(2), 24-36 mo and $10-20M BEFORE Phase 2 opens
US RLD status uncertain - needs formal FDA listed-drug determination (cheap, necessary, nobody has done it)
Nitro reduction at Eh -200 mV plausibly destroys the pharmacophore - settleable by one anaerobic stability assay

Wrong compartment (C2, three serial low-efficiency steps) AND wrong selectivity - its actual primary pharmacology is protonophore/mitochondrial uncoupling, which will uncouple commensals and colonocytes alike
scores.disposition: Spend $200-400k on three benchtop experiments plus the FDA listed-drug letter before anything else. Expect a negative

new_candidates_q6.question: Approved drugs NOT on the flagged list that hit Tier 1 targets

found: Chenodiol (CDCA), CHEMBL240597, approved 1983 - named in the model's own #11 target row with Preclinical (strong) validation, then omitted from A.2

rejected.reason: Hepatotoxicity warning and cirrhosis restrictions; hepatic impairment is overrepresented in CDI
Taurine conjugate is MORE efficiently recaptured by ileal ASBT, plausibly worsening colonic delivery. Useful as a Stage 0 analytical comparator only
Colonic carcinogenesis risk on chronic exposure; no oral formulation (approved as submental-fat injectable)

cspc_germination_tier1_7_11.conclusion: The germination space contains exactly TWO viable approved drugs - ursodiol and chenodiol - and they are stereoisomers of each other. A thin bench; test both in Stage 0

rejected.reason: Gold(I) soft electrophile - fails identically to ebselen in a thiol-saturated lumen, plus nephrotoxicity and blood dyscrasias
Thiol-reactive disulfide; section 6.2 explicitly flags disulfides as unstable at Eh -200 mV

tcdb_cpd_tier1_26.conclusion: NO approved-drug option. But finding two independent thiol-reactive chemotypes failing for the identical reason upgrades the ADMET agent's molecule-specific objection to a CLASS RULE - see cross_cutting_findings

rejected.reason: Non-selective - would adsorb the CDI-treatment antibiotic alongside the inciting one. DAV132's entire engineering exists to solve this; off-the-shelf charcoal is not a shortcut to it
WRONG DIRECTION - these PRESERVE beta-lactam activity; #70 requires DESTROYING it in the lumen. Clean example of the mechanism-direction error the skill file guardrails warn about

luminal_antibiotic_inactivation_tier1_70.conclusion: #70 is the clearest white space in the disease: clinical proof-of-concept exists (ribaxamase Phase 2b positive), no approved drug, no active sponsor. Basis for the in-licensing recommendation

found: Odevixibat (CHEMBL4297588) / maralixibat (CHEMBL363392) as DELIVERY ENABLERS for UDCA
secondary_bile_acid_restoration_tier1_64.conclusion: Surfaced and then rejected on a mechanistic veto - see scores rank 6

other_targets_considered_and_rejected.reason: Doubly disqualified - tolevamer FAILED Phase 3 at luminal sequestration, and 6.2 forbids co-administration (they bind vancomycin and would bind any bile-acid candidate, i.e. they directly antagonise the #66 strategy)
Dose-limiting diarrhoea; narrow therapeutic index; severe toxicity in renal impairment; CYP3A4/P-gp DDIs. Every one lands on a 3.4 population vulnerability
Heart-failure warnings; CHF is prevalent in this population

Effect size almost certainly too small to be a therapy. NOT a candidate, but worth one line as a near-free adjunct arm or stratification covariate in whatever trial runs - #54 is the only host target with any clinical (observational) CDI data
Injectable, expensive, neoplasia warning; wrong risk profile for an acute infection
No Hsp90 inhibitor has ever been approved - all oncology programs failed. Cyclosporine hits the pathway but is DDI-prohibitive
Top of the luminal physicochemical screen and exactly the wrong answer - broad-spectrum destruction of the commensal guild

cross_cutting_findings.title: Targets #46 and #47 are mutually incompatible
cross_cutting_findings.detail: #46 instructs INHIBIT IL-23; #47 instructs AGONIZE IL-22 as a protective epithelial axis. IL-23 is the principal driver of ILC3-derived IL-22, so blocking IL-23 suppresses IL-22. These targets cannot both be pursued. The Round 1 scoring exercise scored candidates independently against a target list and had no mechanism for detecting this.
cross_cutting_findings.consequence: Ustekinumab is not merely unsupported in CDI - it points at the wrong end of an axis the model itself calls protective
cross_cutting_findings.routed_to: Pathway Analyst (Phase 2) - adjudicate whether pathogenic IL-23-driven Th17 inflammation and protective ILC3-derived IL-22 are separable by timing, cell type or magnitude. Until resolved, no IL-23-directed candidate should score positively. Disease model 5.3 should carry an explicit cross-reference between rows #46 and #47

cross_cutting_findings.title: Soft-electrophile covalent chemistry is a CLASS-LEVEL failure in the CDI lumen
cross_cutting_findings.detail: The ADMET agent argued this for ebselen from selenium chemistry. Auranofin (gold, at target #21) and disulfiram (disulfide) fail identically, upgrading a molecule-specific objection to a class rule: any warhead whose mechanism is exchange with a cysteine thiol will be consumed by mM free cysteine, glutathione and bacterial H2S at Eh -200 mV before reaching a target, and will have no selectivity if it does
cross_cutting_findings.consequence: The warhead replacement at #26 cannot simply be 'a different covalent warhead'. It must resist exchange with abundant small-molecule thiols - which rules out most of the standard covalent toolkit
cross_cutting_findings.routed_to: SAR Analyst - narrows the search to reversible-covalent chemistry (fast off-rate vs small thiols, slow vs target), non-covalent CPD inhibitors, or a mucosally-activated prodrug. Hand over as a constraint, not a suggestion

cross_cutting_findings.title: Bile acid pharmacology and CDI share an adverse-event axis
cross_cutting_findings.detail: UDCA, chenodiol, IBAT inhibitors and colchicine all have diarrhoea as their principal or dose-limiting adverse effect. CDI's primary endpoint is diarrhoea recurrence
cross_cutting_findings.consequence: Three protocol requirements for any bile-acid CDI program: (1) toxin-confirmed adjudicated endpoint, never symptom-based; (2) blinded independent endpoint committee is mandatory, not optional - functional unblinding risk is real; (3) dose escalation is doubly constrained, by the adverse effect AND, for UDCA, by the high-dose PSC harm signal. The intuitive answer to 'colonic concentration may be sub-therapeutic' (give more) is closed off from both directions. This is the tightest constraint on the pipeline's leading candidate and was not stated in Round 1

cross_cutting_findings.title: In CDI, in-licensing may beat repurposing
cross_cutting_findings.detail: The Clinical Landscape agent found 6 of 12 CDI failures were financial, not scientific. Read from a repurposing seat that is a shopping list, not a warning: ribaxamase (Ph2b positive, stalled for funding), NTCD-M3 (Ph2 positive, never advanced), CP101 (Ph2 positive, discontinued for financing) are clinically de-risked and financially orphaned
cross_cutting_findings.consequence: Ribaxamase scores 7.4/10 - the highest in this analysis - and is the only asset addressing Tier 1 target #70. A serious CDI strategy should evaluate acquiring one of these alongside, probably ahead of, repurposing a generic bile acid

cross_cutting_findings.title: The project's approved-drug data is stereochemistry-blind, which is disqualifying for bile acids
cross_cutting_findings.detail: CHENODIOL, URSODIOL and DEOXYCHOLIC ACID share a byte-identical descriptor row in chembl_approved_drugs.csv (MW 392.58, AlogP 4.48, TPSA 77.76, HBD 3, HBA 3). UDCA and CDCA differ only in the stereo layer of the InChIKey (RUDATBOHQWOJDD-BSWAIDMHSA-N vs RUDATBOHQWOJDD-UZVSRGJWSA-N)
cross_cutting_findings.consequence: Any descriptor-based or Lipinski-style similarity screen over this dataset treats a germination inhibitor and a secondary bile acid as the same molecule, and ranks cholic acid - the germinant precursor - as a near neighbour of its own antagonists. Bile acid activity in CDI is entirely a stereochemistry and hydroxylation-pattern story
cross_cutting_findings.routed_to: Chemist, SAR Analyst, Natural Product Scout - screen on SMILES/InChI stereochemistry or 3D pharmacophore, never on tabulated descriptors, for this compound class

cross_cutting_findings.title: Physicochemical luminal screening does not find CDI drugs
cross_cutting_findings.detail: Screening 2,973 scorable approved drugs for a luminal-confinement profile (MW>600 OR TPSA>150) returns 403 hits, topped by aminoglycosides, cephalosporins and diagnostic dyes - every one of which would flatten the commensal guild
cross_cutting_findings.consequence: Empirically confirms 6.4: colonic delivery is necessary but nowhere near sufficient; SELECTIVITY is the binding constraint. Any future repurposing screen must filter on commensal-sparing spectrum BEFORE luminal physicochemistry - for which, per Round 1 gap #8, no candidate has measured data

cross_cutting_findings.title: The Ethnobotany agent's bioavailability inversion has a boundary
cross_cutting_findings.detail: 'Compounds abandoned for poor bioavailability elsewhere should be positively screened for CDI' is right for C1 luminal candidates and WRONG for C2 candidates. Niclosamide is the counterexample
cross_cutting_findings.consequence: Refined rule: invert bioavailability scoring only AFTER establishing which compartment the target sits in

cross_cutting_findings.title: The project has no CDI target-drug or gene-disease dataset
cross_cutting_findings.detail: chembl_drug_mechanisms.csv is ~10 rows, chembl_drug_targets.csv ~40 rows, and disgenet__OM_*.csv plus ttd_drug_target_genes.csv are Oral-Mucositis-specific. The systematic target-overlap workflow in the skill file is not executable for CDI
cross_cutting_findings.consequence: Every CDI target assignment in this pipeline rests on the disease model's hand-curated section 5 master list with no database backing

disagreements_with_round1.round1: mean 6.4, Target Profiler 8.5; framed as a repurposing candidate with a fast path
disagreements_with_round1.p2_position: Repurposing feasibility 4.0. No RLD means a full 505(b)(1) NDA, 9-12 yrs, $125-225M. Prior human exposure is not reference-able safety data. The Target Profiler's 8.5 is correct ABOUT THE TARGET and should be preserved as such
It is the primary obstacle. The target is intracellular; solubility ~1.6 uM caps free drug below the active range
Mechanistically contraindicated (CC1) plus PK too slow for an 8-week window
Do not pursue. DDI profile is disqualifying in this population and there is no endpoint

disagreements_with_round1.item: Repurposing as the fastest route (implicit in the skill file itself)
disagreements_with_round1.p2_position: Partly false in CDI. In-licensing a de-risked, financially orphaned Phase 2 asset is faster and better-evidenced

recommended_actions.decides: Whether the fastest path is a transaction rather than a repurpose

derisking_note: Roughly 5% of the cheapest development program in this report, and it resolves Round 1 gaps #5, #6, #7 and most of #2

strategic_fork.question: Who pays? Every top-ranked candidate is a cheap generic and CDI's dominant failure mode is financial

fork_a_speed.description: IR ursodiol, marketed formulation, no IP moat
fork_a_speed.funder: NIAID / BARDA / DoD / CARB-X / academic consortium / payer-funded pragmatic trial
fork_a_speed.outcome: A guideline recommendation for a generic. Maximum patient benefit, zero commercial capture

fork_b_defensibility.description: Proprietary colon-targeted bile acid formulation, composition-of-matter plus method-of-use IP
fork_b_defensibility.outcome: An ownable product. Slower, and carries the PPI-defeats-pH-coating technical risk

strategic_fork.recommendation: Fork A, because the stated objective is fastest path to patients, not best return. But state the tradeoff plainly - Fork A will not attract industry capital, and a program with no owner is exactly how CDI assets die

verify_list: Niclosamide US listed-drug/RLD status (discontinued but referenceable?) - determines whether it has any 505(b)(2) path
Chenodiol current US marketing status and label (Chenodal; Ctexli for CTX) - RLD availability plus the hepatotoxicity/diarrhoea rates quoted
High-dose UDCA PSC harm signal (28-30 mg/kg/d, increased death/transplant) - the most load-bearing single fact in the UDCA assessment
UDCA and CDCA anti-germination IC50 values in C. difficile - Stage 0's go/no-go criterion
Fecal bile acid concentrations in UDCA-treated patients - may be partly answerable from literature before spending $2M
Ebselen clinical development status and sponsors (Daiichi; Sound Pharmaceuticals SPI-1005) - confirms the no-RLD finding
Obeticholic acid current market and regulatory restrictions
Nitazoxanide CDI trial data - size, comparator, outcomes; plus any sporulation/toxin-suppression data. Nitazoxanide's whole case rests on this and its rank would move most
Ribaxamase asset status and Theriva's disposition - whether the in-licensing recommendation is actionable
Orphan designation precedent for recurrent CDI - worth 7 years, stacks with QIDP
disclaimer: All repurposing hypotheses are computational and knowledge-based. No new experimental data was generated. Target-drug assignments derive from the disease model's hand-curated section 5 master list, which has no database backing in this project's current data. Feasibility scores measure development-path tractability, NOT probability of clinical benefit. The verify_list must be cleared before any external-facing use.
